record_type_quote: To validate this association, here we performed replication studies using Japanese and Singaporean case-control cohorts (Japan: 6 cases and 206 controls; Singapore: 22 cases and 178 controls).

targets.authors: Nakano MH, Udagawa C, Shimo A, Kojima Y, Yoshie R, Zaha H, Abe N, Motonari T, Unesoko M, Tamura K, Shimoi T, Yoshida M, Yoshida T, Sakamoto H, Kato K, Mushiroda T, Tsugawa K, Zembutsu H.
targets.title: A genome-wide association study identiﬁes ﬁve novel genetic markers for trastuzumab-induced cardiotoxicity in Japanese population.
targets.evidence_quote: Through genome-wide association study (GWAS), we previously identiﬁed ﬁve single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) as possible genetic susceptibility factors for the risk of trastuzumab-induced cardiotoxicity among Japanese patients. To build on this, here we investigated whether these associations could be further validated in another Japanese population and in a Singaporean population.
targets.outcome_quote: No signiﬁcant association was observed for any of the ﬁve SNPs with trastuzumab-induced cardiotoxicity in these independent cohorts. The diﬀerences in allelic frequencies between this and previous studies might be responsible for the replication failure.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly call the independent-cohort results replication failure. Same-direction estimates and stronger associations after pooling with the original do not supersede that verdict. Small sample size is discussed as a limitation, not a declaration that the attempt cannot adjudicate.
